verdicts.note: Verified: nay on ESSB 6346 final passage (one of eight House Democrats) and on ESSB 5814; yea on ESSB 5813, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5801; yea on 12 of the 65 rejected 6346 amendments. He split even on the two progressive high-earner taxes (nay on the 6346 income tax, yea on the 5813 capital-gains increase), so 0 medium holds.

Supply and permit-streamlining statement [S2] plus nay on the House and conference versions of EHB 1217. Missed counter-evidence in the cited roll calls [S17]: on 2025-04-23 he voted yea on concurring in the Senate version, a looser 10 percent + CPI cap with a single-family exemption, which failed 48-50. So he backed enacting some cap, just not the stricter versions. -1 medium still describes the lean, but the dossier Record line ('nay on House passage ... and on final passage') should add the concur vote.

The $35 insulin cap, lower drug prices and steering patients to primary care [S1][S2] are pole_a's own examples ('cap drug prices ... within existing structures'). With no single-payer statement, -1 medium holds.

Checked rollcalls-1296.xml: besides yea on House third reading (2025-03-12) and final passage as amended by the Senate (2025-04-24), Bronoske voted nay on all ten contested Republican floor amendments roll-called on 2025-03-12 that would have added to the I-2081 rights list (e.g. Burnett 382, monthly evening/weekend curriculum review; 39-42 yeas each), and yea only on two near-unanimous ones (Couture 428, immediate notification of alleged staff sexual misconduct, 93-0; Barkis 462, right to request charter-school enrollment, 92-1). That is not a mixed record: every split vote went toward school discretion, and the two consensus yeas only argue against +2, which was not given. +1 high stands on recorded votes. The dossier should add the amendment votes under Parents and schools.
'I have great concern about the increased taxes enacted' [S1]: clear direction with no named tax or pledge. -1 medium is correctly modest for a single pamphlet sentence.

'Olympia has a spending problem' and 'lack of fiscal responsibility', and the statement makes spending its central reason to replace incumbents [S1]. That is a full pole_a framing, so -2. One statement keeps it at medium.
Pamphlet lists only a school parent board and an HOA presidency [S1]. The dossier and race blurb say plainly that the write-in route is inferred, not confirmed by a by-name tally.
